A defined_relationship involves at least two things with each in a particular role. These turn out to be classifications where the member is the thing playing the role, and the classifier is the role played. Notice the B[2:?] on the involves relationship type. This means that rather than a set of classifications , it is a bag of classifications , where in a bag the same element may appear more than once. This allows relationships that are reflexive and symmetric to be supported. A defined_relationship is a member_of exactly one kind_of_relationship_with_signature that provides the definition of the defined_relationship . A kind_of_relationship_with_signature has a bag of two or more class that are the roles played by the related objects where the class here is also the class in a classification that is involved in the defined_relationship .

Implementer note: The \involves\" relationship is intended to be a Bag (as opposed to a Set).  We have implemented this as a Universally restricted property with a minimum cardinality of 2 but this is not a good implementation of a \"Bag\" as it will default to a \"Set\".  This may not matter, depending on the implementationand use of the data model but is a shortcoming of this approach to representing a Bag in OWL."

A spatio_temporal_extent is some arbitrary piece of space-time that is not necessarily contiguous and is part_of at least one possible_world . A spatio_temporal_extent may have a beginning event and an ending event (it will necessarily have both, but you will not necessarily know them).\n\nA spatio_temporal_extent may be a member_of one or more class_of_spatio_temporal_extent , which in turn may be a member_of one or more class_of_class_of_spatio_temporal_extent . In later diagrams I do not make explicit subtypes of class_of_class_of_spatio_temporal_extent , but this diagram makes them available. A class_of_spatio_temporal_extent may have one or more part__of_by_class relationships to another class_of_spatio_temporal_extent where a member_of one has a member_of the other as a part.
A relationship where each member__of the subclass is a member__of the superclass.
A relationship type where each specialization has exactly one class as a subclass
A relationship type where each specialization has exactly one class as a superclass

A thing is (or can be) anything that exists (as data) and is the ultimate supertype of all the other entity types in the model. The immediate subtypes of thing are individual and abstract_object . The “1” on the subtype graph means that these two entity types are mutually exclusive. A spatio_temporal_extent is distinct as a region of spacetime, while an abstract_object exists in neither space nor time (it is universal). A thing may be a member__of a class . An abstract_object may be either a class or a relationship , but a relationship may not also be a class.

data_EntityName set to optional to allow for the creation of instances of things where the name is unimportant or where assigning a name may create ambiguity.  Use of data_EntityName is to be discouraged once the hqdm sign and pattern naming pattern is employed in systems using this model.

This is an approximation of the Entity-Relationship model called HQDM, generated with known consistency issues (largely due to EXPRESS - OWL notation differences and logic framework mismatches).  Where direct mapping was not feasible sticking to the original model in EXPRESS was favoured over internal consistency within this OWL model.  Please ask the authors if you are interested in the differences. Some references relating to these points have been left as comments in the OWL. The HQDM data object library can be used without making use of hqdm.owl but it has been provided to allow an approximately consistent representation of all of HQDM-based model and user data, including type restrictions.
